cells.tense: You are seeing what is actually in front of you, all the way through, and holding steady while you do.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you have fully understood, to someone who will hear it, and give the same account to yourself that you gave them.
cells.core:
You see how a thing works, not just its surface, and you can keep at it while pressure is on. The whole shape shows up before you say a word, which is why your word is worth waiting for. You finish the read and you stay in the room while it lands — no rush to explain it away, no need to prove you got there first. You hold what you see without turning it into a verdict on anyone.

Nothing has to be fixed. You do not have to prove anything by doing more. Your understanding does not need to become a big explanation; it needs to land where it can be used. Let the next thing you pick up be one you chose, then let it be carried.
cells.sheetLine: You see it clearly and you hold steady while it lands.
cells.verb: seeing a thing all the way through to the end
cells.place: where what must be carried is borne without breaking

cells.tense: You are holding a shape you are sure about before the thing itself is done forming.
cells.ask: Take one thing you are almost sure about and leave it undecided for a day, on purpose, then decide with what the day gave you.
cells.core:
By the time someone is halfway through, you have finished it for them, and what you spend on the unfinished part does not get counted anywhere. The certainty is doing work; it has also gotten ahead of the thing itself. You end up bracing for a version that hasn't happened, and the effort goes there instead of here.

Nothing has to be broken. What you are sure about is real. The guess just arrives early and loud enough that the guess becomes the thing. Take one thing you are almost sure of and leave it open a day, then decide with what the day brought. No one has to agree with you for this to mean something. You are the one who gets to be surprised.
cells.sheetLine: The guess arrived before the thing finished forming.

cells.tense: You saw how it all works, said nothing, and now you stand at a moment that has moved on without you.
cells.ask: Write one sentence about something you noticed and put it in front of one person, without softening it first.
cells.core:
You saw how it worked, and you did not take it anywhere. Under any real demand you go tense or go blank, and you cannot stand in the moment long enough to use what you see. You went quiet somewhere back and have not come back to the room where the present happens. What can bear weight in you is unexercised, so it reads as not there.

You are not empty. Write one sentence about something you noticed and put it in front of one person without softening it first. Hold what they give back without turning it into a verdict. Small and specific. The next thing you say does not have to be the whole thing.
cells.sheetLine: You saw it. You left the room before you said it.

cells.tense: You are keeping your head under pressure and calling it something that happens on its own.
cells.ask: Name one thing you held back today, out loud to yourself, and say which part of it was your choice.
cells.core:
You are keeping your head, not letting the moment throw you — and you talk about it like the pressure is something that happens to you. Nobody has to be thanked. But your hand is on it, and that part goes unclaimed. When you say it just got handled, your own part of it disappears.

You are steadier than you tell yourself. Name one thing you held back today, out loud to yourself, and say which part of it was your choice. That is all. It does not make you the strong one or the fixed one. It just puts the pen back where it already is, which is what a next small choice is.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding that line. Say so.

attempts.check: The draft's one unsupported move is 'people bring you things because you steady what they're holding' — the record says holding capacity, not that others seek the person out; better to say only what the person holds. A reader could reasonably say the Balanced cell sounds like praise for being the strong one, and the Too Much cell could flatten into pestering instead of the guess that the whole shape is known before it exists. The ask survives a wrong read in every cell: showing one thing as it is, leaving one blank, saying one word, doing the small next step are all usable even if the seat is wrong. The sentence that serves the writer and not the person is anything like 'you have always carried more than your share' — cut the history, keep the act.
